children: Infrastructure investor Infratil beats with its 1H earnings, sending its share price up 3.7% to NZ$13.69. Jefferies says proportionate Ebitdaf was 10% higher than consensus hopes, although likely more skewed to 1H than in prior years. The beat was driven by better-than-expected results at data-center unit CDC, telecoms business One NZ and Longroad Energy. Infratil also upgraded its annual guidance for proportionate operational Ebitdaf, which excludes corporate costs, by 2.6%. It now forecasts a range of NZ$1.37 billion-NZ$1.44 billion. Analyst Roger Samuel notes the revised guidance is around 1% below consensus forecasts for NZ$1.405 billion at the midpoint of the range. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
